title: Arriving From Between
notes: Expanded from v4 by scene generator. Added sub-locations for Room 3327, missing locations (Tesla household after Dane, Gospic valley fields, Port of New York 1884, Wardenclyffe evidence), and script-weighted props (Dane's coat, shoes, tin fork, Do Not Disturb sign, letter of introduction, headboard rail). All existing v4 entries preserved.

assets.name: Alice_Monaghan_1943
assets.physique: Irish-American woman, late 30s, medium build, dark hair pinned under a white maid's cap, practical posture, composed expression trained by years of hotel service
assets.attire: Hotel New Yorker maid uniform — white blouse, black dress, white apron, white cap, black leather shoes
assets.notes: Housekeeping staff. Found Tesla's body on the morning of January 8, 1943. Smelled the ozone before she crossed the threshold. Told no one officially except her sister, once.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1943
assets.notes: Age 86. Final day. Found dead in Room 3327, Hotel New Yorker. Sheets pulled to military tightness. Three gray-tipped feathers on the windowsill. Hotel napkins covered in equations on the desk.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Newborn infant, pale skin, dark hair, eyes open at the moment of birth
assets.notes: Born at stroke of midnight during a violent lightning storm in Smiljan. FLUX cannot render infant Tesla from training data — needs description.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1859
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 3 years old, slight frame, dark hair, large dark eyes, small hands spread flat on the cat's back
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, loose trousers, bare feet
assets.notes: The cat scene. Pulled a sheet of sparks from Macak's back in a dark room. Responded with a question, not fear. FLUX needs description for child-age Tesla.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1862
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 6 years old, thin build, dark hair, intense focused eyes, holding a tin fork at the dinner table
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, braces, dark trousers
assets.notes: The geometry vision scene. Fork in hand at dinner table when the visual field was replaced by luminous squares. FLUX needs description for child-age Tesla.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1884
assets.notes: Age 28. Arrived at Port of New York with four cents and a letter of introduction to Thomas Edison.

assets.name: Duka_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Serbian woman, mid-30s, strong peasant build, dark hair pulled back tightly, weathered hands, intense dark eyes, high cheekbones, broad shoulders from farm work
assets.attire: Simple white linen dress for childbirth, wool blanket over shoulders
assets.notes: Tesla's mother, née Mandic. Known for exceptional memory — could recite Serbian epic poetry at length. Built her own household tools. Gripped the wooden headboard rail during labor with the focus of someone doing something with all of themselves.

assets.name: Milutin_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Serbian Orthodox priest, late 30s, tall, lean build, full dark beard, deep-set eyes, high forehead, scholarly bearing
assets.attire: Black Orthodox clerical robe with silver cross pendant
assets.notes: Tesla's father. Parish priest of Smiljan. Spoke four languages. Could parse Greek and Latin scripture. Named what his son pulled from the cat's back: electricity. The same thing as lightning.

assets.name: The_Midwife_1856
assets.physique: Croatian village woman, approximately 61 years old, stout and sturdy build, grey hair beneath a white kerchief, calloused hands, practical weathered face, expression of someone who has seen the work of birth and death without flinching
assets.attire: Simple brown wool dress, white apron, leather shoes
assets.notes: Unnamed village midwife who delivered Tesla. Had lived on the Lika plateau for 61 years. Hair on her forearms stood straight up crossing the threshold. Sparks jumped from her skirts with every step. Described to her daughter that the smell in the house was the smell of lightning that had already struck — while the lightning was still in the sky.

assets.name: Zdravko_Blazic_1856
assets.physique: Croatian schoolteacher, mid-30s, lean build, neat dark hair, ink-stained fingers, observant eyes behind a practical expression, the look of a man trained to write down what he sees
assets.attire: Simple wool coat, white shirt, dark trousers, leather boots
assets.notes: Schoolteacher in Gospic valley, 15 kilometers below Smiljan. Kept a meticulous diary of weather, road conditions, and livestock. His July 1856 entry described livestock standing in open fields facing the same direction, the well water tasting different, and the morning light looking like an examination being conducted. The exact date is water-damaged in the surviving page.

assets.name: Subject_K_1974
assets.physique: Croatian woman, approximately 80 years old, small and thin, white hair, careful deliberate speech, the bearing of someone carrying something she has been deciding whether to pass on for decades
assets.attire: Simple dark dress, wool shawl, practical shoes
assets.notes: Identified only as Subject K. in a 1974 cassette interview with a graduate student from the University of Zagreb. Third-generation memory carrier. Her grandmother was a young woman from Gospic in 1856 who described the sky looking clean in a way it hadn't been before the morning after Tesla's birth. Died before 1990. No family named.

assets.name: Dane_Tesla_1863
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 12 years old, taller and heavier than Nikola, dark hair, confident bearing of the celebrated eldest son
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, dark trousers, worn leather shoes that had been broken in precisely to his foot's shape
assets.notes: Tesla's older brother. Died in a horse accident in Smiljan, approximately 1863-1865 (sources disagree). His coat remained on the hook by the door. His shoes held the shape of a foot that would not return. After his death, Tesla's visions intensified in frequency and vividness.

assets.name: Walter_Simmons_1943
assets.physique: American man, early 40s, medium build, practical work-worn face, steady observant eyes, the unhurried bearing of someone who has walked the same building corridors for years
assets.attire: Hotel maintenance uniform — grey coveralls or work trousers and jacket, heavy leather work boots
assets.notes: Maintenance worker at the Hotel New Yorker from approximately 1935 to 1950. Kept a diary of the building's physical life. In January 1943, during routine rounds on the 33rd floor, smelled ozone in the corridor near Room 3327 despite it being January with no storm. Noted it in his diary and walked on. His diary ends with that January 1943 entry. His initials and partial diary survive in a typescript provided to a researcher in the 1960s; the researcher died before the book was published. The foundation holding the estate papers does not maintain a public finding aid.

assets.name: PE_Foxworth_1943
assets.physique: American man, late 30s, clean-shaven, sharp jaw, close-cropped dark hair, military bearing in a civilian suit, alert eyes that do not settle
assets.attire: Dark grey wool suit, white shirt, narrow tie, fedora, leather briefcase
assets.notes: FBI Assistant Director. Head of the Special Intelligence Service. Was involved from early on January 7, 1943 — before Tesla's body was publicly reported. His timeline of involvement precedes the publicly established discovery timeline.

assets.name: John_G_Trump_1943
assets.physique: American man, mid-30s, round face, receding hairline, wire-rimmed glasses, academic softness, mild expression that does not match the weight of what he was asked to evaluate
assets.attire: Tweed suit jacket, bow tie, white shirt, leather oxfords
assets.notes: MIT physicist assigned to review Tesla's seized papers. Reviewed 60 years of work in three weeks. Concluded the material did not include new workable principles for scientific or military application and would not constitute a hazard in unfriendly hands. The material was then classified for decades.

assets.name: Hotel_New_Yorker_1943
assets.notes: Art deco hotel, 43 stories, corner of 34th Street and 8th Avenue, Manhattan. Tesla's home for his final decade, given to him at a nominal or free rate in exchange for the distinction of his residence.

children.name: Room_3327_1943
children.physique: Corner room on the 33rd floor. Heavy curtains, still against the cold winter light. Dark wood desk positioned near the window. Single bed against the north wall, sheets pulled to military tightness. Hotel napkins stacked on desk and bedside table and scattered on the floor, covered in dense mathematical notation that crosses the paper edges without registering them as limits. Radiator ticking beneath the window. Three gray-tipped feathers on the windowsill, arranged as if placed. The room colder than the corridor — the cold of a space that has not had a living body moving through it. The air carries the smell of a summer storm in January.
children.notes: Wide establishing shot of the full room. Room number divisible by 3. Tesla's requirement. The window was left open for the white pigeon. The Do Not Disturb sign had been on the door for three days before Monaghan opened it.

children.name: Room_3327_Desk_Area_1943
children.physique: Dark wood writing desk positioned near the window of Room 3327. The desk surface completely obscured by dozens of white hotel napkins covered in dense mathematical notation in pencil — a handwriting that crosses the printed borders of the napkins without adjusting, treating the paper's edges as limits the mind declined to recognize. A draft from the window left open in January stirs the napkins slightly. Pencil stubs, a magnifying lens, a water glass with a residue ring. The desk lamp unlit. Natural winter light from the window falling across the equations. The windowsill with three gray-tipped feathers visible at the periphery.
children.notes: The desk is where Tesla did his final work. The napkins are the only writing surface available in quantity. The equations are real mathematics — active scientific work, not scribbling. The desk appears in close-ups AND in wider room shots — must be visually consistent in both.

children.name: Room_3327_Windowsill_1943
children.physique: The windowsill of Room 3327, wide enough to hold objects. Three gray-tipped feathers lying at angles that suggest placement — deliberate, considered arrangement, not the casual landing of shed feathers. The window itself slightly ajar despite January cold, heavy curtains hanging still on either side. Through the gap: the grey winter light of Manhattan morning, the geometry of buildings across 8th Avenue. Condensation on the glass where warm room air meets cold window. The radiator ticking beneath, its iron surface patinated with decades of repainting.
children.notes: The window was left open for the white pigeon. She was not coming back. He knew she was not coming back. The feathers were on the windowsill despite the window being closed and undisturbed when Monaghan entered — but Tesla had been keeping the window open for years. The feathers are from a pigeon dead for approximately 20 years.

children.name: Room_3327_Bed_1943
children.physique: Single bed against the north wall of Room 3327. Sheets pulled to a specific tightness — not hotel housekeeping tightness but the precision of someone who understood this would be the last arrangement and made it accordingly. White linens, thin wool blanket folded with geometric exactness. A bedside table with more hotel napkins covered in equations. On the floor beside the bed: additional napkins, some crumpled, some laid flat as if referenced during the night. The pillow showing the slight depression of a head that rested with intention.
children.notes: The body was arranged with a precision that did not suggest rest. Alice Monaghan's professional composure broke here — not dramatically, not with sound, but in a breath.

children.name: Room_3327_Door_Threshold_1943
children.physique: The interior of Room 3327 as seen from the doorway — the view Alice Monaghan had when the door swung inward. The Do Not Disturb sign hanging from the interior handle. The corridor light spilling in behind, mixing with the cold winter light from the window ahead. The full depth of the room visible: desk to the left near the window, bed against the far wall, the shape under sheets barely registering at this distance. The smell — sharp, clean, metallic — moving outward through the open door into the corridor as if concentrated air finding an opening.
children.notes: This is the threshold moment — the boundary between the ordinary hotel corridor and whatever was in that room. The smell did not wait for her to step into it. It stepped into her.

children.name: Hotel_Corridor_33rd_Floor_1943
children.physique: Long narrow hallway, repeating pattern of dark wood doors. Geometric carpet in muted burgundy and gold. Flat institutional lighting from wall sconces. Brass room numbers on each door. Quiet. Still. The smell of ozone detectable near Room 3327 — the kind of smell that arrives after a summer storm — in a building with sealed windows in January.
children.notes: Where Walter Simmons noticed the smell during his regular maintenance rounds.

children.name: Hotel_New_Yorker_Exterior_1943
children.physique: 43-story art deco tower at the corner of 34th Street and 8th Avenue. Brick and limestone facade with strong vertical emphasis. Hotel New Yorker signage near the crown. Street-level awnings. January snow on sidewalks. Yellow taxicabs on 8th Avenue. Pedestrians in winter overcoats and hats.

assets.name: Smiljan_Village_1856
assets.physique: Small village on a high limestone plateau in the Lika region of the Austrian Empire's Military Frontier. Rocky karst landscape, cold even in summer. Stone farmhouses with dark timber roofs and whitewashed walls. A single road through the village. A Serbian Orthodox parish church at the center. Wild thyme growing between the stones. Summer night — dense warm air, limestone dust smell, distant thunder.
assets.notes: Modern-day Croatia. Population under 400 in 1856. The Tesla family farmhouse was adjacent to the parish church where Milutin Tesla served as priest.

children.name: Tesla_Farmhouse_Smiljan_1856
children.physique: Simple stone farmhouse with whitewashed walls and dark timber roof. Small windows with wooden shutters. Bare earth yard. Oil lamp light visible through the window. The smell of the storm outside penetrating the walls — sharp, clean, electric. Interior: rough stone walls, low timber ceilings, oil lamp casting uneven light.
children.notes: Where Tesla was born at the stroke of midnight, July 10, 1856, during a violent lightning storm.

children.name: Tesla_Birthing_Room_1856
children.physique: Small interior room lit by a single oil lamp. Rough stone walls, low timber ceiling. A bed with linen sheets. A washing basin on a wooden stand. Hair on arms standing up from atmospheric charge. Sparks jumping from fabric to floorboard. The air thick with the smell of lightning — metallic, copper-edged, sharp — despite the storm being outside.
children.notes: The smell in the room was the smell of lightning that had already struck, while the lightning was still in the sky.

children.name: Tesla_Dark_Room_1859
children.physique: A dark interior room in the Tesla farmhouse. No lamp lit. Night. A three-year-old boy sitting with a large family cat on his lap, hands spread flat on the animal's back. The fur warm under small palms. Complete darkness until the sheet of sparks erupts — blue-white, continuous, fanning from tail to neck, illuminating the child's own finger bones from beneath.
children.notes: The cat Macak scene. Approximately 1859 when Nikola was age 3.

children.name: Tesla_Dining_Room_1862
children.physique: Family dining room in the Tesla farmhouse. A table set for a meal. The ordinary sonic texture of family dinner — conversation, the clatter of tin utensils. A boy of approximately 6 holding a tin fork, the seam where handle meets tines detectable under his thumb. The room as it appears before the vision: warm, occupied, ordinary. Then the visual field replaced entirely by perfect luminous squares tessellated across every surface.
children.notes: Where Tesla first experienced the geometry vision at approximately age 6, circa 1862.

children.name: Tesla_Household_After_Dane_1863
children.physique: The interior of the Tesla farmhouse after Dane's death. The same rough stone walls, the same low timber ceilings — but every room the wrong size. Not smaller. Wrongly proportioned. Too large. The walls in the same positions, the ceiling the same height, the furniture unmoved — but something that filled them is no longer filling them. By the door: a coat on a hook, hanging slightly differently because the person who will take it down is no longer coming. Worn leather shoes beside the door, broken in to the exact shape of one boy's foot. The absence has gotten into the objects. It has affected their relationship with gravity.
children.notes: After Dane Tesla died (~1863-1865, sources disagree), the house changed. Not physically — proportionally. The coat and the shoes are the script's central images for grief as a spatial phenomenon. Tesla's visions intensified after this loss — the aperture through which the geometry arrived seemed to have widened.

assets.name: Gospic_Valley_1856
assets.physique: Valley town 15 kilometers below Smiljan on the limestone karst road. The valley floor visible from the plateau above. Open fields surrounding the town. Livestock normally pressed against fences and enclosures during storms. The morning after the birth storm: open fields with livestock standing in the open, all facing the same direction. The light that morning described as an examination being conducted — very white and particular, not the ordinary summer light of the Lika region.
assets.notes: Where Zdravko Blazic kept his diary and the Austrian Imperial Meteorological Institute maintained an observation station.

children.name: Blazic_Schoolhouse_1856
children.physique: A modest schoolteacher's quarters or private room in Gospic. A writing desk by a window. Ink and quill. A diary open to a freshly written entry. The window facing the valley fields where the livestock stood. Predawn light becoming the strange examination-quality morning light of July 11, 1856.
children.notes: Where Blazic recorded his observations of the livestock, the well water, and the light quality the morning after Tesla's birth.

children.name: Austrian_Meteorological_Station_1856
children.physique: Small observation station — a stone or timber outbuilding with a barometer, thermometer, and early atmospheric instruments mounted on stands. A log book open on a writing surface. A margin notation in a hand different from the standard observer's — different pen, different pressure. The instrument showing an anomalous reading that was checked and re-checked and could not be explained.
children.notes: The Austrian Imperial Meteorological Institute maintained a station in Gospic as part of its network. The margin note reads: atmospheric ionization reading anomalous this morning. Instrument rechecked. No instrument fault found. There is no follow-up entry.

children.name: Gospic_Valley_Fields_1856
children.physique: Open fields on the valley floor below Smiljan at dawn on July 11, 1856. The storm has passed. The sky carries a quality described as an examination — very white and particular, not the ordinary summer light of the Lika region. Livestock standing in the open fields, all facing the same direction. Not east, not toward town, not toward shelter. Every animal oriented the same way, as if addressed by something that had arrived or was arriving. Fences and enclosures visible but unused — the animals have moved into the open voluntarily. Morning mist on the karst limestone. The examination-light falling on everything with equal, assessing weight.
children.notes: Blazic recorded this at dawn. The livestock did not shelter during the storm — they moved into the open. Every animal facing the same direction. He wrote it with the sentence structure of a man writing quickly, before the mind's need for explanation could smooth the image into comfort.

assets.name: Hotel_St_Regis_1922
assets.notes: Where Tesla was living in 1922 when the white pigeon died in his hands. He was at the St. Regis before further financial unraveling brought him eventually to the Hotel New Yorker.

children.name: Tesla_Hotel_Room_St_Regis_1922
children.physique: Hotel room interior, 1920s. A man in his mid-60s holding a dying white bird with gray-tipped wings. The bird's weight shifting from held to carried. The room ordinary in every respect except for the light that came from the pigeon's eyes in the moment of her death — described as more powerful and blinding than anything Tesla had produced in his laboratory.
children.notes: The moment the white pigeon died. O'Neill recorded Tesla's account of a real light, powerful and blinding, more intense than the most powerful lamps in his laboratory.

assets.name: Port_Of_New_York_1884
assets.physique: The immigration arrival area at Castle Garden (later Ellis Island), New York Harbor, June 1884. Wooden docks, iron railings, the bustle of immigrant processing. A tall young man of 28 with sharp features stepping onto American soil. Four cents in his pocket. A letter of introduction folded in his coat. The harbor behind him — tall-masted ships, steam vessels, the skyline of lower Manhattan. The specific weight of arriving somewhere with nothing but the contents of your own mind.
assets.notes: Tesla arrived June 6, 1884. He had been running machines in his mind for years before this crossing — complete, functional, mechanical systems operated entirely behind his eyes. He carried almost nothing physical. The letter was to Thomas Edison.

assets.name: Wardenclyffe_Evidence_1943
assets.physique: Not Wardenclyffe Tower itself — but the EVIDENCE of Wardenclyffe found in Room 3327 and seized materials. Architectural drawings on yellowed paper showing a tower designed to transmit power wirelessly. Correspondence with J.P. Morgan on faded letterhead. Financial records showing the gap between what was promised and what was funded. Photographs of the tower before demolition — the distinctive mushroom-shaped copper dome atop the skeletal wooden framework. All found among Tesla's papers, all part of what was seized.
assets.notes: MANIFEST-ONLY RULE: Wardenclyffe Tower is not a visitable location in this episode. It is referenced through documents, drawings, and photographs found in manifest locations (Room 3327, seized trunks). Show the evidence of Wardenclyffe, not Wardenclyffe itself.

assets.name: Macak_The_Cat_1859
assets.physique: Large Serbian farm tomcat. Dark-striped fur, heavy body. Back broad enough for a three-year-old to press both hands flat against. In darkness, the fur erupts with a continuous sheet of blue-white sparks fanning from the base of the tail to the neck when stroked — illuminating the child's finger bones from beneath for one instant before returning to darkness.
assets.notes: The family cat. Mačak is the Serbian word for tomcat. The discharge from his fur is what prompted Milutin Tesla to name electricity for his son for the first time.

assets.name: White_Pigeon_1922
assets.physique: A white pigeon, pure white with light grey tips on her wings. Small body — lighter than appearance suggests, the feathers making the size while the body beneath is much smaller. She made a habit of Tesla's window and returned daily. When dying: held in two large aged hands, the small body still warm, the grey-tipped wings spread slightly, the eyes producing a light more intense than any lamp in Tesla's laboratory.
assets.notes: Tesla described her to biographer O'Neill: a beautiful bird, pure white with light grey tips on her wings. He described finding recognition in her gaze — the only recognition in 86 years of looking. He loved her as a man loves a woman, and she loved him. When she died, something went out of my life. And then: Up to that time I knew with a certainty that I would complete my work.

assets.name: Three_Gray_Tipped_Feathers_1943
assets.physique: Three feathers on the windowsill of Room 3327. Each feather primarily white with gray tips. They do not lie as if drifted there or shed casually. They lie at angles relative to each other that suggest placement — deliberate, considered arrangement.
assets.notes: Found by Alice Monaghan when she entered Room 3327 on January 8, 1943. The white pigeon had been dead for approximately 20 years. The feathers were on the windowsill despite the window being closed and undisturbed.

assets.name: Tesla_Hotel_Napkin_Equations_1943
assets.physique: Dozens of white hotel napkins covered in dense mathematical notation in pencil — equations in a handwriting that crosses the printed borders of the napkins without adjusting, that treats the paper's edge as a limit the mind declined to recognize. Found on the desk, the bedside table, and the floor beside the bed. The equations are real mathematics — active scientific work, not scribbling.
assets.notes: Tesla used hotel napkins as his primary writing surface in his final years. The work showed no mental deterioration. The equations crossed the paper's edges as if the physical limits of the surface were irrelevant to the thinking being recorded.

assets.name: Tesla_Seized_Trunks_1943
assets.physique: Twenty trunks — worn leather steamer trunks with brass clasps, reinforced wooden crates bound with wire, cardboard filing boxes. Mixed sizes. Labels in mixed English and Serbian handwriting in Tesla's personal shorthand, dates spanning six decades. The accumulated output of a working mind that had not stopped until it stopped entirely: notes, designs, private correspondence, objects of investigation.
assets.notes: Seized by the Office of Alien Property Custodian within approximately two days of Tesla's death. Reviewed by John G. Trump in three weeks. Declared harmless. Then classified for decades.

assets.name: OAPC_Pre_Labeled_Crates_1943
assets.physique: New wooden shipping crates of raw unfinished pine slats, splintery. Stamped with official government markings in black ink: OFFICE OF ALIEN PROPERTY. Serial numbers. Pre-labeled before Tesla's death — the dimensions calibrated for what they intended to take, as if the inventory had been measured in advance.
assets.notes: The agents arrived with these crates already prepared and labeled. Empty. Already fitted for transport. Pre-labeling crates is not a response to death — it is preparation for an expected event.

assets.name: Blazic_Diary_1856
assets.physique: A handwritten diary, leather-bound, pages filled with a schoolteacher's careful script. The writing has the patient texture of a man recording the observable world for its own sake — weather, road conditions, livestock counts. One page water-damaged, the date partially illegible. A July 1856 entry describing livestock behavior, well water taste, and the examination-quality light of the morning of July 11. Transcribed in a 1931 regional folklore pamphlet that exists in no national archive.
assets.notes: Zdravko Blazic's diary. The July 1856 entry was written quickly, before the mind's need for explanation could smooth the image into comfort. He wrote it and moved to the next day's entry: road conditions.

assets.name: Atmospheric_Ionization_Log_1856
assets.physique: A formal observation log from the Austrian Imperial Meteorological Institute's Gospic station. Standard printed columns for atmospheric pressure, temperature, and precipitation filled in with careful bureaucratic handwriting. In the margin of the July 11, 1856 entry: a notation in a different hand, different pen, different pressure on the nib — written by someone who did not sign. The margin notation is the only anomaly in an otherwise standard record.
assets.notes: The margin note reads: Atmospheric ionization reading anomalous this morning. Instrument rechecked. No instrument fault found. Will report if anomaly continues. There is no follow-up entry. The note was written by a second observer who did not sign and never followed up.

assets.name: Dane_Coat_On_Hook_1863
assets.physique: A boy's coat hanging on a wooden hook by the door of the Tesla farmhouse. Simple dark wool, worn at the elbows, the fabric holding the shape of shoulders that wore it daily. It hangs slightly differently now — not because the hook has changed or the coat has changed, but because the person who will take it down is no longer coming to take it down. The absence has gotten into the coat. It has affected its relationship with gravity.
assets.notes: Dane Tesla's coat. After his death, it remained on the hook. The script uses it as the central image for how grief changes ordinary objects — not through any visible alteration, but through the withdrawal of the future that gave them purpose.

assets.name: Dane_Worn_Shoes_1863
assets.physique: A pair of worn leather shoes beside the door of the Tesla farmhouse. Broken in exactly the way one person's foot breaks leather — the slight asymmetry of how Dane stood, the particular weight distribution of how he walked, the specific shape of heel and arch and toe pressed into the leather over years of wearing. The shoes have learned their wearer. They hold the shape of someone who is not there.
assets.notes: Dane's shoes. Shoes learn their wearer with the patience of an object that spends years in close contact with a specific body. The body was not coming back. The shoes did not know this.

assets.name: Tesla_Tin_Fork_1862
assets.physique: A tin dinner fork, heavy for a child's hand. Slightly warm from being held. The seam where the handle was joined to the tines detectable under the thumb — a small ridge the thumb finds and returns to. Cold on the first touch, body-warm within sixty seconds. An ordinary object with the specific weight of the ordinary world — the last thing the six-year-old Tesla held before the geometry vision replaced his entire visual field.
assets.notes: The fork from the geometry vision scene. Tesla was holding it when his visual field was replaced by blinding light and then luminous geometric squares. The fork was still in his hand when he returned. The tactile world had not gone anywhere. Only the visual field had been replaced.

assets.name: Do_Not_Disturb_Sign_1943
assets.physique: A standard Hotel New Yorker cardboard door hanger, slightly curved from years of hanging. Dark printed border, the hotel's art deco design. Hanging from the brass door handle of Room 3327. It had been there since approximately January 5 — three days. The guest management record noted that the occupant had not requested food, laundry, or any contact whatsoever. This was known to be a preference. Longstanding. Staff had been told.
assets.notes: Three days on the door. The sign is both a practical hotel object and the first piece of evidence — the first indicator that something had changed behind this door. Staff knew not to disturb. But three days was three days.

assets.name: Tesla_Letter_Of_Introduction_1884
assets.physique: A folded letter on cream-colored paper, handwritten, addressed as an introduction to Thomas Edison. The paper worn at the folds from being carried in a coat pocket across an Atlantic crossing. The handwriting of someone who expected this letter to open a door. Alongside it: four American cents — the total cash Tesla carried when he arrived at the Port of New York on June 6, 1884.
assets.notes: Tesla arrived with four cents and this letter. He had been running machines in his mind for years before the crossing — complete, functional, mechanical systems operated entirely behind his eyes. The letter was his only physical credential. Everything else was internal.

assets.name: Birthing_Room_Headboard_Rail_1856
assets.physique: A wooden headboard rail on a simple bed in the Tesla birthing room. Dark timber, worn smooth where hands have gripped it. Duka Tesla's grip marks — not the grip of a frightened woman but of someone doing something with all of themselves. The wood shows the impression of fingers that held with a focus the midwife recognized as total commitment. Sparks from the charged air occasionally jumping to the wood surface.
assets.notes: The headboard rail Duka gripped during labor. The script describes her grip as requiring everything available — the grip of commitment, not fear. The midwife's hands found their positions. The work was clear, even when the room was wrong.

assets.name: FBI_Declassified_Tesla_File_1943
assets.physique: A thick government file, more than three hundred pages. Manila folder with typed labels, classification stamps, and declassification markings. Pages of typed reports, handwritten notes, memoranda between agencies. The FBI's file on Nikola Tesla — publicly available through the FBI's online FOIA reading room. The pages carry the institutional weight of a government that seized eighty trunks of material, declared it harmless, and then classified it for decades.
assets.notes: The FBI's declassified Tesla file runs more than 300 pages. Anyone can read it. The individual contents of the approximately eighty trunks and crates remained classified for decades. Harmless things are not classified.
